reason: The passage depicts conflict rather than collaboration between the leader (Saul) and the people (David). Saul actively seeks to kill David ('מְבַקֵּשׁ אֶת־ נַפְשִׁי' - 'seeks his life'), and Jonathan must work secretly against his father to protect David. Jonathan helps David escape through deception and covert planning (the arrow signal), which demonstrates division and antagonism between the leader and the young man, not open collaboration and cooperation.
